initial.title: [v0.92.1][C-SDLC v2][bug] Reject stacked closing publication without a GitHub closing relation
initial.goal: Prevent C-SDLC v2 publication from recording terminal closing authority for stacked pull requests when GitHub does not expose the target issue through closingIssuesReferences.
initial.required_outcome: Closing-mode csdlc-publish fails closed unless live GitHub PR readback confirms the exact target issue through closingIssuesReferences, and stacked checkpoint publication remains explicitly non-closing.
authority_boundary: Issue #645 owns the C-SDLC v2 publication guard for stacked closing relation readback
PR #644 is reproducer evidence only and must not be retargeted or merged by this issue
GitHub closingIssuesReferences is the live authority for terminal closing linkage
Typed C-SDLC v2 remains the lifecycle authority
operator_constraints: Do not merge, retarget, or mutate PR #644
Do not use raw gh as a lifecycle write workaround
Do not weaken body keyword validation
Do not write tracked issue work on main
Do not use AWS, paid provider APIs, big runners, or live provider inference
initial.task_boundary: Repair the typed C-SDLC v2 publication/readback path so stacked PRs without a GitHub closing relation cannot be recorded as terminal closing publication.
deliverables: Closing-mode publish guard that requires exact live closingIssuesReferences linkage
Typed publish/PR-state agreement on linked_issue, linkage_source, base, head, and linkage mode
Explicit fail-closed guidance for stacked/non-default-base closing publication without a GitHub relation
Regression test for the PR #644 shape
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Closing-mode publication fails closed when live GitHub readback does not expose the target issue through closingIssuesReferences.
AC-2: A non-default stack-base PR cannot be recorded as closing publication unless GitHub reports the exact closing relation.
AC-3: Typed publish result and typed PR-state result agree on linked_issue, linkage_source, base, head, and linkage mode.
AC-4: Stacked checkpoint work has explicit non-closing/dependency mode and cannot masquerade as terminal closing authority.
AC-5: The failure message tells the operator whether to wait for the dependency branch merge, publish against the default branch, or choose the non-closing checkpoint route.
AC-6: A regression test covers the PR #644 shape: body starts with Closes #631, base is non-default, and GitHub closing relation is absent.
dependencies: Current C-SDLC v2 GitHub PR-state closingIssuesReferences parser
non_goals: Do not merge, retarget, or otherwise mutate PR #644
Do not close or rewrite issue #631 lifecycle truth
Do not replace GitHub closingIssuesReferences authority with body parsing
Do not implement C-SDLC v3 publication cutover
Do not run live provider, AWS, paid, or big-runner validation
initial.plan_summary: Bootstrap and bind #645, reproduce the typed publication mismatch with offline test fixtures and current live read-only PR state, add the fail-closed closing relation guard, and validate the C-SDLC v2 publication lane.

steps.action: Bind #645 into a FastWork issue worktree and confirm live read-only PR #644 still has no GitHub closing relation.
Add or tighten the csdlc-publish closing-mode reconciliation guard against live PR-state linked_issue/linkage_source.
Preserve explicit non-closing checkpoint semantics for stacked dependency PRs.
Run focused C-SDLC v2 publication regression tests, formatting, and diff hygiene.

invariants: GitHub closingIssuesReferences is required for terminal closing authority
Body keyword parsing remains necessary but not sufficient
Non-default stack-base PRs fail closed unless GitHub reports the exact closing relation
Checkpoint/dependency publication is explicit and non-terminal
risks: A helper may still infer linked_issue from PR body after the guard is added
Existing publish tests may assume body keyword validation alone is enough
Non-closing checkpoint paths may need clearer linkage-mode output to avoid overclaim
Live GitHub API shape could differ from offline fixtures
stop_conditions: The issue cannot be bootstrapped or bound without writing tracked work on main
The live PR-state relation cannot be verified read-only
The fix requires mutating PR #644 or bypassing typed lifecycle writes
Focused regression tests cannot model closingIssuesReferences absence deterministically

validation_lanes.proof_role: Prove closing-mode publication rejects a non-default-base PR whose body has a closing keyword but whose GitHub closing relation readback is absent.
Confirm Rust formatting and diff hygiene for the changed publication surfaces.

initial.failure_policy: Fail closed on missing live GitHub closing relation, ambiguous linkage source, non-default-base terminal overclaim, raw gh lifecycle workaround, stale PR-state truth, or zero-test validation.
review_prompts: Can csdlc-publish still record a terminal closing publication when GitHub closingIssuesReferences is absent?
Does the regression test cover the PR #644 stacked-base shape rather than only body parsing?
Do publish and PR-state outputs agree on linked_issue and linkage_source?
Is non-closing checkpoint publication clearly non-terminal?
Does the failure message give the operator actionable stack/default/checkpoint choices?
initial.review_scope: C-SDLC v2 publication and PR-state linkage semantics for stacked PRs, live closingIssuesReferences authority, fail-closed diagnostics, and offline regression coverage only.
